messages:
vijay: Heads-up: noticed a cluster-wide flurry of ECC/Xid spikes in us-west-2 over the last 24h, lots of transient alerts. Here's a quick rollup of patterns I saw: short 1-2s spikes on different cards, often coinciding with heavy batch jobs.
claire: Yep saw that too. Most were single-sample blips from DCGM exporter. They're firing our node drains which is killing capacity during peak. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
jen: Are the exporter sample rates different across pools? we recently bumped some to 1s for perf metrics.
vijay: Good call — us-west GPU pools have sample_interval=1s. I suspect noisy counters + sampling noise = false positives.
sam: Can we debounce in prometheus rules rather than changing sample rates? draining is expensive.
claire: I'd rather try rule-side smoothing first. Proposal: add a recording rule with a moving_average over 5 samples, plus a 'for' window to require sustained errors.
vijay: Draft rule I tested locally:

```yaml
- record: dcgm:ecc_xid_err_rate:avg5
  expr: avg_over_time(dcgm_gpu_ecc_xid_errors[10s])

- alert: GPU_ECC_XID_Sustained
  expr: dcgm:ecc_xid_err_rate:avg5 > 0
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained ECC/Xid errors on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```

This turns many of the 1-2s blips into non-alerts.
jen: Nice. Two quick thoughts: 1) use avg_over_time with a range that aligns with scrape_interval (eg 30s if scrape) to avoid off-by-one. 2) consider a second tier alert (warning) for short spikes so we still log but don't drain.
vijay: Agreed. I tested with scrape=15s; used 5 samples => 75s window. Might be safer to keep warn/page split.
sam: Also add a coalescing rule across cards on same host so we don't page for 1 card among 8. Something like: sum by (instance)(dcgm:..)>0 and threshold>2
claire: Sketch:

```yaml
- alert: GPU_MultiCard_ECC
  expr: sum by (instance)(dcgm:ecc_xid_err_rate:avg5) >= 2
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

This prevents single-card noise causing a host drain.
infra-bot: deploy-plan created by vijay: dcgm-rule-smoothing/v1 -> canary to us-west-2-gpu-pool
jen: Can we run canary in a single AZ and monitor false-positive rate + capacity impact for 48h? Also record cost metric: drained_capacity_gpu_hours.
vijay: Yup will canary to az-1 small subset. I'll attach a dashboard: false-positive rate, drain count, and preemptible reclaim rate.
sam: One more: add note in runbook about when to override (eg real ECC bursts coinciding with PCI resets). We should keep an emergency escape hatch to lower 'for' quickly.
claire: I'll update the runbook and add escalation play for persistent Xid > 30/min.
jen: Great. Next steps: vijay do canary, collect 48h metrics; if FP drops >= 80% and capacity saves >5%, promote.
vijay: On it. Will post results here and open a PR for the rules with test vector traces. Thanks all :thumbsup:
